34738.subject: Commerce
34738.question_text: The development of trade in West Africa was aided by the
34738.explanation: Portuguese expansion into Africa began with the desire of King John I to gain access to the gold-producing areas of West Africa. The trans-Saharan trade routes between Songhay and the North African traders provided Europe with gold coins used to trade spices, silks and other luxuries from India

34739.subject: Commerce
34739.question_text: An issuing house is an outlet for
34739.explanation: Issuing house. a financial institution  that arranges and underwrites the issue of new STOCKS and SHARES on behalf of corporate clients on the STOCK EXCHANGE.

34740.subject: Commerce
34740.question_text: Which of the following is quoted when the buyer is responsible for the cost of loading the goods from the seller's warehouse up to his own warehouse?
34740.explanation: "Free Alongside Ship" means that the seller fulfils his obligation to deliver when the goods have been placed alongside the vessel on the quay or in lighters at the named port of shipment. This means that the buyer has to bear all costs and risks of loss of or damage to the goods from that moment.

34741.subject: Commerce
34741.question_text: The relationship between all imports and exports of a country is known as
34741.explanation: Balance of trade is the difference in value between a country's imports and exports.

34743.subject: Commerce
34743.question_text: Which of the following is an example of large-scale retailing?
34743.explanation:
Large-Scale Retailers 

  •  Mail Order Sale:
  • Consumer Co-Operative Stores:
  • Vending Machine:
  • Discount Houses:
  • Supermarket (Self-Service Store):
  •  One-Price Shop:
  • Departmental stores

34744.subject: Commerce
34744.question_text: A cheque drawn by a bank on itself is a/an
34744.explanation: A bank draft is a cheque drawn by a bank on its own funds.

34745.subject: Commerce
34745.question_text: A voluntary body formed by people in the same line of business for the purpose of protecting their interest is a
34745.explanation: Trade association is an association of people or companies in a particular business or trade, organized to promote their common interests.

34746.subject: Commerce
34746.question_text: Those who are engaged in the distribution of goods belong to
34746.explanation: Commercial Occupation: This refers to all the people involved in the distribution and exchange of goods produced by the industrial sector. Examples of commercial workers are: bankers, transporters, insurers, traders, etc.

34747.subject: Commerce
34747.question_text: When an insurance policy is declared void because of a false declaration ; the principle involved is
34747.explanation: The doctrine of utmost good faith is a principle used in insurance contracts, legally obliging all parties to act honestly and not mislead or withhold  important information while entering the contract

34748.subject: Commerce
34748.question_text: Buildings and machinery used in the running of a business are examples of
34748.explanation: Fixed assets are assets which are purchased for long-term use and are not likely to be converted quickly into cash, such as land, buildings, and equipment.

34749.subject: Commerce
34749.question_text: Which of the following is classified as invisible item in balance of payment?
34749.explanation: The invisible balance or balance of trade on services is that part of the balance of trade that refers to services and other products that do not result in the transfer of physical objects. Examples include consulting services, shipping services, tourism, salaries of expatriates and patent license revenues.

34750.subject: Commerce
34750.question_text: Collecting information on the taste of consumers and the extent of demand for a product is
34750.explanation: market research; is the action or activity of gathering information about consumers' needs and preferences.

34751.subject: Commerce
34751.question_text: Which of the following is not an insurance of indemnity
34751.explanation: Indemnity insurance is a contractual agreement in which one party guarantees compensation for actual or potential losses or damages sustained by another party. The life insurance is not part of indemnity insurance because life cannot be restored once lost.

34752.subject: Commerce
34752.question_text: The entitlement of a debenture holder from a company's income is known as
34752.explanation: debentures are a long-term security yielding a fixed rate of interest, issued by a company and secured against assets. The holders are paid a fixed interest

34753.subject: Commerce
34753.question_text: The collection of tariffs on imported goods is the function of
34753.explanation:
Functions of customs and excise authorities

  • Collect and revenue for the government by charging customs and excise duties.
  • Collect, keep and analyse records of imported and exported goods and services.
  • Control bonded warehouses to ensure that duty is collected on imported dutiable goods before releasing them

34754.subject: Commerce
34754.question_text: A licensed person who is authorized to sell to the highest bidder is
34754.explanation: An auctioneer is a person who manages an auction, or a public sale at which people can bid on items. Goods are sold to the highest bidder in an auction.

34755.subject: Commerce
34755.question_text: An efficient transport system enables a trader to
34755.explanation: It enable a trader to distribute goods to a wider market range.

options.text: widen the market for his products

34756.subject: Commerce
34756.question_text: The Central Bank's monetary policy instrument by which it buys and sells treasury bills is known as
34756.explanation: Open market operations (OMO) refers to when the Federal government through the central bank purchases and sells Treasury securities on the open market in order to regulate the supply of money that is on reserve in banks, and therefore available to loan out to businesses and consumers.

34757.subject: Commerce
34757.question_text: Which of the following acted as the central bank for West African countries before their independence?
34757.explanation: The West African Currency Board was established in October 1912 following the Report of a Departmental Committee set up by the Secretary of State to enquire into the currency in use in British West Africa. It served as a central bank for the member states

options.text: The British Bank for West Africa

34758.subject: Commerce
34758.question_text: Current account holders withdraw money by means of
34758.explanation: Current account holders use cheques to withdraw money from their bank accounts. A cheque is an order to a bank to pay a stated sum from the drawer's account, written on a specially printed form.

34759.subject: Commerce
34759.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of mail order business?
34759.explanation:
Following are the salient features of a mail order business:

(1) This business does not require much capital.
(2) The business can be carried even without owning a shop, sitting at house.
(3) In a mail order business there is no need of middlemen, as the goods are directly sent to the customers by post.

34760.subject: Commerce
34760.explanation: Bonded warehouse is a customs-controlled warehouse for the retention of imported goods until the duty owed is paid.

34761.subject: Commerce
34761.question_text: Which of the following is concerned with promoting favorable image of an organization?
34761.explanation: Public relations; the professional maintenance of a favourable public image by a company or other organization or a famous person.

34762.subject: Commerce
34762.question_text: The document issued by the registrar of companies to permit a public limited company to commence business is
34762.explanation: A certificate of incorporation is a legal document/license relating to the formation of a company or corporation. It is a license to form a corporation issued by state government or, in some jurisdictions, by non-governmental entity/corporation.

34763.subject: Commerce
34763.question_text: Which of the following is not an economic grouping
34763.explanation:
Economic grouping is an organization that encourages economic cooperation among its member countries. The The Lake Chad Basin Commission is not an economic grouping. 

The Lake Chad Basin Commission is an intergovernmental organization that oversees water and other natural resource usage in the basin.

options.text: Economic Community of West African States

34764.subject: Commerce
34764.question_text: One of the principles of insurance is
34764.explanation: Proximate cause is an insurance principle that refers to the first event, or first peril, in a series of events that cause damage in an insurance claim.

34765.subject: Commerce
34765.question_text: A written instruction by a current account holder to his bank to debit his account at regular intervals with a specified amount for a given period is known as
34765.explanation: standing order; an instruction to a bank by an account holder to make regular fixed payments to a particular person or organization.

34766.subject: Commerce
34766.question_text: A collective bundle of shares is called?
34766.explanation: Stock is the capital raised by a company or corporation through the issue and subscription of shares. Summation of shares is referred to as stock

34767.subject: Commerce
34767.question_text: The assets of a business that is available for cash or near cash is called
34767.explanation: Liquid capital is defined as cash or items which are readily converted to cash in a short time.

34768.subject: Commerce
34768.question_text: The bank on which a cheque is drawn is known as the
34768.explanation: Drawee is a legal and banking term used to describe the party that has been directed by the depositor to pay a certain sum of money to the person presenting the check or draft. The bank that cashes your check is the drawee, your employer who wrote the check is the drawer, and you are the payee.

34769.subject: Commerce
34769.question_text: A percentage reduction from the quoted price of goods given to a buyer to encourage bulk purchase is called
34769.explanation: A trade discount is a percentage reduction from the quoted price of goods offered to encourage bulk purchases or to promote trade with certain buyers.

34770.subject: Commerce
34770.question_text: The difference between the cost price and selling price of an article is
34770.explanation: Mark-up is simply the amount added to the cost price of goods to cover overheads and profit. This is the difference between the buying price and the selling price

34771.subject: Commerce
34771.question_text: A ceiling on the quantity of commodity to be imported into the country is called
34771.explanation: Quota; is a limited quantity of a particular product which under official controls can be produced, exported, or imported.

34772.subject: Commerce
34772.question_text: The buyer in a hire purchase contract becomes the legal owner of the goods by paying
34772.explanation: Hire purchase is a system by which one pays for a thing in regular installments while having the use of it. The buyer becomes the overall owner of the property when the last installment has been paid.

34773.subject: Commerce
34773.question_text: The document which helps in ascertaining the correct value of imports in order to assess the custom duty is
34773.explanation: ships manifest; is simply a list of the shipments or cargo that a vessel is carrying

34774.subject: Commerce
34774.question_text: The combination of product, price, promotion and distribution decisions employed by a company is referred to as
34774.explanation: marketing mix; is simply a combination of factors such as product, price, promotion and place that can be controlled by a company to influence consumers to purchase its products

34775.subject: Commerce
34775.question_text: The document which specifies the manufacturer from whom goods are to be imported is
34775.explanation:
A closed indent restricts the agent to a named manufacturer from whom the goods must be bought while an open indent gives the agent a free hand in obtaining the goods from any source

In other words, an open indent is an order to an overseas purchasing agent to buy certain goods, without specifying the manufacturer. If the manufacturer is specified this is a closed indent

34776.subject: Commerce
34776.question_text: Who among the following generally has no capacity to enter into a valid contract
34776.explanation: The general rule regarding contracting with minors or infants is that such a contract is voidable by the minor. This rule has been established to protect younger individuals who may not fully grasp the consequences of certain contracts. Minors are believed to lack the capacity to contract.

34777.subject: Commerce
34777.question_text: The satisfaction of customers in all business activities is emphasized by
34777.explanation: The marketing concept is the philosophy that firms should analyze the needs of their customers and then make decisions to satisfy those needs, better than the competition.

34778.subject: Commerce
34778.question_text: The document which is used when a country imposes ad valorem duties is
34778.explanation:
Ad valorem; (is the levying of tax or customs duties) proportionate to the estimated value of the goods or transaction concerned. They extend to taxes such as import duty taxes on goods from abroad. 

The main purpose of a consular invoice is to provide a complete and detailed description of the goods to the foreign customs authority, so as to ensure that the correct import duty is levied on the goods.

34779.subject: Commerce
34779.question_text: An activity involving buying, selling, distribution of goods and services is known as
34779.explanation: Generally, commerce refers to the exchange and distribution of goods, services or something of value, between businesses or entities.

34780.subject: Commerce
34780.question_text: Which of the following arrangement of documents is the correct sequence as used in the retail trade? i. Quotation ii. Enquiry iii.Order iv Invoice
34780.explanation:
The sequence goes thus; enquiry => quotation => order => invoice 

A buyer sends an enquiry to the seller asking about the goods he wants to purchase

The seller send the buyer a quotation containing products description, prices etc

The buyer then places an order

The seller sends an invoice to the buyer as prove of a business transaction

34781.subject: Commerce
34781.question_text: Mr Lou who assured his life with XYZ Assurance Company, was involved in an accident and had a broken leg; the sum of #80,000 was paid to Mr Lou for his broken leg. The money received is known as
34781.explanation: Indemnity insurance is a contractual agreement in which one party guarantees compensation for actual or potential losses or damages sustained by another party. Mr Lou was indemnify at the tone of N80,000

34782.subject: Commerce
34782.question_text: The size of of profit of a business is measured by the
34782.explanation: Rate of turnover: Is the number of times a firm sells out its merchandise or finished goods inventory

34783.subject: Commerce
34783.explanation: Industrial Occupation: This involves those who engage in the physical production of goods or changing of raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods or products.

options.text: growing and extraction of raw materials

34784.subject: Commerce
34784.question_text: The abbreviation E & O.E. on an invoice seeks to
34784.explanation: This is an abbreviation for "errors and omissions excepted," a disclaimer stating that information in a document is not necessarily accurate. It is used to say that a price list, product description, or other document may contain mistakes or may not include some details

options.text: draw the attention of the buyer to the contents of the document
show that there is no error about price quoted on the invoice
protect the seller against any error on the document
draw the attention of the seller to the contents of the document

34785.subject: Commerce
34785.question_text: The functions of credit and thrift society does not include
34785.explanation: Cooperative thrift and credit societies can address some of the shortcomings of Esusu. These are member-based organisations that help members to address economic problems. The ultimate goal is to encourage thrift among the members and to meet the credit needs of people who might otherwise be exposed to exploitation. Their functions does not include option D

options.text: charging low interest rate on loans

34786.subject: Commerce
34786.question_text: Throwing cargo overboard in order to save a ship from sinking is
34786.explanation: Jettison; this simply means to throw or drop (something) from an aircraft or ship.

34787.subject: Commerce
34787.question_text: The document in which full details of goods and the ship carrying the goods are contained is known as
34787.explanation: A Certificate of Origin (CO) is an important international trade document that certifies that goods in a particular export shipment are wholly obtained, produced, manufactured or processed in a particular country.

34788.subject: Commerce
34788.question_text: The exclusive right of an author over his book is
34788.explanation: Copyright; is the exclusive and assignable legal right, given to the originator for a fixed number of years, to print, publish, perform, film, or record literary, artistic, or musical material.
